raw_response:
Answer: D
Reason: Malignant mesothelioma is classically associated with asbestos exposure, evidenced by pleural calcifications (plaques), and presents as a pleural-based mass causing a homogenous opacity with an obtuse angle to the chest wall; the presence of pleural nodules further supports this diagnosis over simple effusion or parenchymal disease.
